texts.value: The small GTPases Rab are key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking, from the formation of transport vesicles to their fusion with membranes. Rabs cycle between an inactive GDP-bound form and an active GTP-bound form that is able to recruit to membranes different sets of downstream effectors directly responsible for vesicle formation, movement, tethering and fusion (By similarity). RAB6C may be involved in the regulation of centrosome duplication and cell cycle progression

location.value: Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton, microtubule organizing center, centrosome

texts.value: Highest levels are found in fetal and adult brain, prostate, testis and spinal cord. Undetectable expression in adrenal gland, skeletal muscle, bone marrow, fetal, and adult liver, heart, salivary gland, and trachea. Detected in the HEK293, HEK293T, LNCaP, MCF-7, T-47D and EVSA-T cell lines (at protein level)

Switch 1, switch 2 and the interswitch regions are characteristic of Rab GTPases and mediate the interactions with Rab downstream effectors. The switch regions undergo conformational changes upon nucleotide binding which drives interaction with specific sets of effector proteins, with most effectors only binding to GTP-bound Rab
